answer: Make every reward depend on a footprint the claimant cannot forge alone: a record accepted by an unrelated outside system — a public archive, an open dataset, a stranger-run service — retrievable by anyone without the claimant's help. A sparrow chattering on the jetty convinces only its own flock, but a juniper cutting must take root in foreign soil under a foreign gardener who can refuse it. One operator can tend a few plantings; a hundred need a hundred different hosts, so cloning multiplies gatekeepers, not rewards.
